crit: the per-Stop scan cost is measured, filed as #127, and its SHAPE pinned -- not implied solved by the worst-case budget
ev: Maintainer asked whether a full-ledger read at every Stop eats context and tokens. TOKENS: bounded by design, measured 1618 bytes / 13 lines in the 100-target worst case (cap is 10 rows x 110 bytes, #93/#94), zero on a clean ledger, ledger never enters context -- nothing to fix. WALL CLOCK: real and NOT addressed by CAPS_MAX_STEPS, which fixed only the 11.1s worst case. Realistic shape (25 ids x 2 criteria = 50 keys, mostly PASS), 5 runs each, whole scan: 48 rows 0.05s, 500 0.12s, 1000 0.4s, 2000 0.8s, 3000 1.2s, 5000 1.9s truncated. So a few thousand rows is 1-2s every Stop. MY FIRST TWO TABLES WERE WRONG: the fixture used 210 distinct keys, over the 100-key ceiling, so every scan truncated early and the timings described PARTIAL work while reading like full scans -- caps_truncated was in the output and I did not read it. Corrected before filing. Filed as issue 127 with the budget-first sequencing (the Stop hook has no stated wall-clock budget the way statusline has CR5 300ms; writing it is step 1), and both cheaper designs REFUSED with reasons in the lib header: a tail window breaks the reset rule (a clearing PASS sits anywhere), an mtime cache has a stale-cache failure mode that is the exact class this file exists to end. Three cases pin the SHAPE not a duration, incl a CONTROL that the fixture stays under CAPS_MAX_KEYS. crit: the step budget now charges the comparisons it performs, and the case for it is not vacuous
ev: Copilot said the charge was off by 1 on hits. MY FIRST TWO CASES FOR IT WERE VACUOUS and the mutation is what said so: draft 1 (hit-only) trips the LINE bound before the STEP bound so both accountings truncate; draft 2 (100 keys x 3000 rows) puts BOTH past the budget at 153450 vs 156550 -- the suite reported 963 passed with the defect restored. Verified BOTH ways: truncated=1 shipped, truncated=0 pre-fix. Two controls: the ledger is under CAPS_MAX_LINES so the STEP bound is what fired, and the same shape under budget does not truncate. crit: the step budget now covers every path, and the stub that hid it mirrors the shipped code
ev: Copilot round 3 found the budget check was SKIPPED on the PASS path: that branch charged its lookup then continued past the test at the loop tail. Root cause of the blind spot: a PASS is NOT cheaper than a FAIL (same linear lookup, only the post-lookup work differs), so the cheap branch was cheap in the wrong dimension; branches merged into one if/elif chain with a single exit, no continue before the guard. crit: the cap report now reaches a channel that exists on exit 0, and a task named Gate is no longer discarded
ev: Codex round 2 found the feature was fully tested and NEVER DELIVERED: a Stop hook's stderr on exit 0 reaches the DEBUG LOG only (documented contract, confirmed against the hooks doc), so the cap report -- the one thing that must be seen when NOTHING blocks -- went to the channel that discards it, visible only when an unrelated gate happened to block. Reproduced: stdout was EMPTY on a tripped allowing stop. No test caught it because every case asserted captured stderr, which is correct for the BLOCKING paths -- a test that a message was PRODUCED is not a test that it was DELIVERED, and when the channel differs per exit code the tests must too. Fix: systemMessage JSON on stdout on the ALLOWING path only, encoded by jq/python3 (untrusted ledger text, and the harness parses stdout on every exit code so malformed output is worse than none); blocking paths keep stderr where exit 2 makes it the channel. Four delivery cases: present, parses with non-empty systemMessage, clean ledger emits NOTHING, blocking stop emits no stdout JSON. COPILOT: header matched by PREFIX discarded any row with id 'Gate' and criterion 'Criterion' -- an id ops-task.sh permits -- measured tripped=0 on two real rework rounds through the CLI; now matched whole (the full header cannot collide, its 4th cell PASS/FAIL is refused by the verdict enum). ops-reverify.sh has the same filter, predates this branch at 65d78e5, filed as #128 not fixed in passing. My bounded-work probe also needed repair: the report_row refactor gave it a second stderr writer so it measured 212 for a 100-byte row while claiming to read the input -- its own control exposed it. crit: a truncated cap scan stops instead of walking a table it has discarded
ev: Copilot's one live thread on PR #126 was real and I measured it before believing it: the key-ceiling branch set caps_truncated=1 and FELL THROUGH, so the loop kept doing full 100-key lookups for every remaining row while feeding a report the truncation rule had already abandoned (a truncated scan returns before building one). Measured on a 20000-row ledger of DISTINCT failing targets -- the shape that hits the ceiling at row 100, and what a project with many one-off task ids looks like: 0.97s before, 0.14s after, 7x. Waste not DoS (the step budget did bound it), so the fix is ONE condition at the loop existing sole exit, not a second break upstream -- the sole-exit shape is what the PASS-path defect cost us three rounds ago. THE CASE ASSERTS ROWS READ, NOT WALL CLOCK: the budget makes durations converge, and this file already paid once for a timing assertion that flaked on GitHub while passing locally. xtrace counts the loop own n=<digits> assignment, unique to the read loop.
